name: Mouloud Feraoun
role: Algerian writer and martyr of the Algerian revolution
contribution: An Algerian writer and martyr of the Algerian revolution born in Tizi Hibel, Kabylie.
legacy: All of his works describe this person's native society – the Berber mountain farmers – and their life, poverty, the love of one's homeland, emigration, and the consequences of French colonialism.

checks.lead: Mouloud Feraoun (Kabyle: Mulud At Ceɛban; 8 March 1913 – 15 March 1962) was an Algerian writer and martyr of the Algerian revolution born in Tizi Hibel, Kabylie. Some of his books, written in French, have been translated into several languages including English and German. In 1951, he corresponded with the Algeria-born French author Albert Camus. He was kidnapped and assassinated by the French OAS on 15 March 1962, just days before the end of the war.
